title: Strict simultaneous DVR reduction models and residue triangles
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $C_n=(R/\varpi^n)_X$ for $n\geq1$, let $q_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$ be the quotient maps, and put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}C_n$ with projections $\pi_n:B\to C_n$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Write $Q$ for localization from cochain complexes of $B$-module sheaves to $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For any $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ there is a K-flat complex $P$ with flat $B$-module terms and an isomorphism $Q(P)\simeq K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Set $P_n=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_n}(P\otimes_B C_n)$, using termwise sheaf tensor and restriction of scalars [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. There are simultaneous isomorphisms $Q(P_n)\simeq K_n:=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_n}(K\otimes_B^L C_n)$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] under which the actual chain maps $t_n=1_P\otimes q_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ are the canonical derived quotient transitions. For every $n\geq1$, the $B$-linear map $u_n:C_1=k_X\to C_{n+1}$ induced on constant coefficients by $\bar r\mapsto\varpi^nr\bmod\varpi^{n+1}$ gives a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of $B$-modules
$$0\longrightarrow P_1\xrightarrow{1_P\otimes u_n}P_{n+1}\xrightarrow{t_n}P_n\longrightarrow0.$$
Consequently there is a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$K_1\longrightarrow K_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\bar t_n}K_n\longrightarrow K_1[1]$$
whose second arrow is the same canonical quotient transition $\bar t_n=Q(t_n)$ under the simultaneous identifications. No completeness, cohomological bound, constructibility, or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $K$ or $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0942, lemma-bounded, proof of (1), displayed ideal-quotient distinguished triangle: DVR specialization with the explicit identification of the successive coefficient kernel with k_X; simultaneous flat-term K-flat realization of that triangle.

proof.text: Choose a cochain complex $G$ and an isomorphism $e:Q(G)\simeq K$, using the localization description in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ and $G$. This gives a quasi-isomorphism $f:P\to G$ with $P$ K-flat and every $P^i$ flat. Fix this single $P$ and the isomorphism $e\circ Q(f):Q(P)\simeq K$ for the entire argument. The resolution theorem applies to any complex on a ringed site, so no boundedness or hypothesis on $X$ is needed.

Write $A_m=R/(\varpi^m)$. The coefficient datum [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] gives $R\subset E$ and $\varpi\ne0$. For $n\geq1$, define $v_n:A_1\to A_{n+1}$ by $\bar r\mapsto\overline{\varpi^n r}$. Changing $r$ by $\varpi s$ changes the image by $\varpi^{n+1}s$, so the map is well defined. If $\varpi^n r=\varpi^{n+1}s$ in $R$, cancellation in the field $E$ gives $r=\varpi s$, proving injectivity. The quotient $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ is surjective, and its kernel consists exactly of the classes $\overline{\varpi^n r}$. Thus $0\to A_1\xrightarrow{v_n}A_{n+1}\to A_n\to0$ is an exact sequence of $R$-modules. If $a\in A_{n+1}$, multiplication by $a$ on its source is through $A_{n+1}\to A_1$, and $v_n((a\bmod\varpi)\bar r)=a v_n(\bar r)$, since both sides are $\overline{\varpi^n ar}$.

source.place: Tag 0942, lemma-bounded, proof (1): elementary DVR calculation identifying the successive kernel

proof.text: Apply the exact constant module functor of [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] with coefficient ring $R$ to the sequence in step 2. By [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor], its objects have underlying constant abelian sheaves, and its arrows are the sheafifications of the actual coefficient maps. Hence the resulting arrows are $u_n:C_1\to C_{n+1}$ and $q_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$, with an exact underlying sequence $0\to C_1\xrightarrow{u_n}C_{n+1}\xrightarrow{q_n}C_n\to0$. To read exactness in the underlying abelian sheaves, use [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], whose forgetful functor preserves kernels and cokernels. This use is on the small skeleton in the module universe prescribed for $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$; it imposes no geometric restriction on $X$.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact; Tags 03DA and 03DB, module forgetful exactness

proof.text: Give all three terms their $B$-actions via the projections. The $A_{n+1}$-linearity identity at the end of step 2 passes to constant module sheaves by the unique extension of the presheaf scalar action in [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. Thus $u_n$ is $C_{n+1}$-linear when $C_1$ has the action through $C_{n+1}\to C_1$. By [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], the projections satisfy $q_n\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n$ and $(C_{n+1}\to C_1)\pi_{n+1}=\pi_1$. Therefore restricting those actions makes $u_n$ and $q_n$ $B$-linear, exactly by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The sequence of step 3 is consequently short exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(B)$: the kernel is the sectionwise kernel and the cokernel is the sheafified sectionwise cokernel, as specified in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; its underlying sequence is already exact. Notice that $u_n$ is a module map, not a unital ring map.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; restriction of actions and coordinate identities of the inverse limit

proof.text: For each integer $i$, flatness of $P^i$ means precisely that $-\otimes_B P^i$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The symmetry isomorphisms of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] therefore make $P^i\otimes_B-$ exact as well. Apply it to the $B$-module short exact sequence of step 4. This gives $0\to P^i\otimes_B C_1\xrightarrow{1\otimes u_n}P^i\otimes_B C_{n+1}\xrightarrow{1\otimes q_n}P^i\otimes_B C_n\to0$. By the sheaf tensor construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the differentials are $d_P^i\otimes1$ and commute with these maps: both composites have value $d_P^i(p)\otimes u_n(c)$, respectively $d_P^i(p)\otimes q_n(c)$, on elementary tensors before sheafification. These are therefore actual chain maps and the displayed rows form the asserted degreewise short exact sequence of complexes. Flatness here is used over $B$, not over $C_n$.

source.place: Tag 03ER, definition-flat, item (3); Tag 03EO, lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor; Section Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product

proof.text: For each $n$, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] applied to $\pi_n:B\to C_n$ and the fixed resolution $f:P\to G$ computes $K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C_n$ by $P\otimes_B C_n$. The comparison of [lem-pe-restricted-kflat-tensor-identification], specialized to $B\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}B\xrightarrow{\pi_n}C_n$, then gives the isomorphism $\alpha_n:Q(P_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$, including the canonical localization comparison for restriction of scalars. Its scalar-swap map and inverse cancel, so it is precisely the scalar-last model $P\otimes_B C_n$ used here. To check the transitions, apply [lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison] to $P$ and the $B$-linear map $q_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$. Its coefficient naturality says that $Q(1_P\otimes q_n)$ corresponds to $1_{Q(P)}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}q_n$. With the same $e\circ Q(f)$ for every $n$, and the restricted change-of-rings comparisons just specified, this is the canonical quotient transition: $\alpha_n Q(t_n)=\bar t_n\alpha_{n+1}$. Thus the identifications are simultaneous; no choices of separate resolutions at different levels occur. The scalar-extension/restriction and compatible reduction-tower constructions are those of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] and [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined]; these are proof-only citations of the interfaces, whose helper definitions are recorded separately for the statement.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 06YU, definition-derived-tor and its preceding construction; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, identity underlying topos

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] in the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ to the degreewise short exact sequence of step 5. It gives a distinguished triangle $Q(P_1)\to Q(P_{n+1})\xrightarrow{Q(t_n)}Q(P_n)\to Q(P_1)[1]$ with the displayed second arrow, not an unspecified arrow between isomorphic objects. Replace its vertices by $K_1,K_{n+1},K_n$ using $\alpha_1,\alpha_{n+1},\alpha_n$ from step 6 and the shifted $\alpha_1$. Distinguishedness is preserved under isomorphisms of triangles by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The second arrow becomes $\alpha_n Q(t_n)\alpha_{n+1}^{-1}=\bar t_n$ by step 6, proving the claimed triangle. All constructions used only the ringed-site resolution, exact constant realization and flatness; they imposed none of the additional hypotheses excluded in the statement.
